title: Carried-workholding check: steel up to one grid pitch into the part at a side face or step passes

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happens.** The carried-workholding check (`app::fixture_carried`, the carried dexel body against a fixture) knows the carried part only at its grid's column centres. At a side face or a step of the carried part, a fixture's steel that reaches into the material by less than one grid pitch, and stops short of the next material column centre, is not refused.

This is not new with PR #1549: main's box law (`penetration`) has the same blind band. The M3 review of PR #1549 measured it (pullrequestreview-5898992751):
- A single box jaw overlapping a part's side face by 0.9 pitch, at 11 phases against the grid: main and the PR agree at every phase (10 refusals, 1 pass where a column centre lies exactly on the jaw face).
- The flipped hat at pitch 0.375: a jaw overlapping by 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 pitch passes on main and on the PR; at 0.9 pitch and more both refuse (`5.00 mm deep`).

**Bound.** By construction under one pitch: steel more than one pitch inside a face covers a material column's lines or lies in a rectangle of four material columns, which PR #1549 reads whole. On the shipped grid (`max(r/8, span/1023)`) that is 0.375 mm on the test stock, about 1 mm on 1 m stock.

**Expected.** Side-face contact resolved finer than one pitch (for example, reading the carried part's own side faces, or a finer local grid where a fixture face lies within a cell of a material boundary), or the bound stated in the refusal law and pinned.

**Done means:** side-face contact is resolved finer than one pitch, or the bound is pinned at several phases of the face against the grid (main's and the mesh reading's verdicts asserted equal, and the passing depth asserted below one pitch).

Refs #1530. Found in the review of PR #1549 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1549).
